target_native_profile.entities: Visitors and visitor groups, the exhibition as a sequenced space, exhibits and objects, interpretive text (entrance panel, labels), visitor routes, stops/pauses, interview statements, interpretive frames or themes visitors voice, visitor prior knowledge and agendas.
target_native_profile.relations: Panel precedes and frames later exhibits (advance-organizer role); exhibits are ordered along routes; dwell time relates to attracting/holding power; interview themes relate to specific exhibits encountered; prior knowledge shapes what is noticed and said.
target_native_profile.processes: Cumulative meaning-making across the visit, shifts of attention, museum fatigue and declining engagement over time, narrative building from sequential encounters, social negotiation of meaning within groups.
target_native_profile.operations: Timing-and-tracking observation of routes and stops, in-gallery or exit interviews, think-aloud or accompanied visits, thematic coding of interview talk, before/after comparison when a label or panel is revised (formative or remedial evaluation).
target_native_profile.observables: Route maps, stop counts and dwell times per exhibit, sequence of exhibits visited, coded interview themes, use of panel vocabulary or concepts in visitor talk, exit summaries of what the exhibition was about.
target_native_profile.inferences: Whether the panel functions as an advance organizer that shapes interpretation; which exhibits gain or lose attention; how interpretive frames develop or shift across the visit; differences in exit understanding between panel versions.
target_native_profile.failure_modes: Different visitor populations in the two periods, self-selection, small samples, observer and interviewer effects, social desirability, seasonal or crowding confounds, novelty effects, coding subjectivity, fatigue confounded with position in route.

source_transfer_profile.entities: The visitor moving through the exhibition is the dynamic system; the entrance panel content is the controlled input; the panel change between periods is the step; interpretation over visit time (from routes, pauses, and interview talk) is the output; the two panel versions define two input levels.
source_transfer_profile.relations: Input drives output through the system; output features are indexed to time since entry (t=0 at panel encounter); the before-period trajectory is the baseline against which the after-period trajectory is a response to the input change; features of the trajectory constrain system properties.
source_transfer_profile.processes: Transient response of interpretation after the panel encounter (onset, rise, possible over-application, correction) moving toward a settled interpretation by exit; steady-state difference between panel versions; decay or persistence of the panel's framing across the visit.
source_transfer_profile.operations: Align each visit on entry as time zero, sample interpretation at points through the visit, build a time-indexed interpretation signal per condition, compare before/after trajectories, and extract temporal features (delay before the frame appears, rise in its adoption, overshoot, oscillation between frames, settling point, exit-level difference).
source_transfer_profile.observables: Time or position at which panel-derived frames first appear in talk (delay); rate of increase in frame usage (rise); over-application of the frame then moderation (overshoot); alternation between frames (oscillation); point at which interpretation stabilizes (settling); exit difference in interpretation between panel versions (steady-state change).
source_transfer_profile.inferences: The panel's influence has a characteristic onset speed, strength, and persistence; candidate models of framing (persistent priming vs decaying priming vs late consolidation) can be distinguished by trajectory shape; exhibition elements act as disturbances or interacting inputs whose effect can be located in time.
source_transfer_profile.failure_modes: Noise (individual variability), unknown initial state (prior knowledge and agenda), saturation (ceiling on frame adoption), nonlinearity (interpretation not proportional to panel content), disturbances (crowding, companions, staff), interacting inputs (other labels), insufficient observation time (short or truncated visits), dependence on operating point (this exhibition only); plus the mismatch that the step is applied across different visitors rather than to the same system.

entities.rationale: Visitors, panel, exhibits, routes, and interviews are all native. Casting the visitor-in-exhibition as a system with an input and an output is a modest extension; the panel already has a recognized input-like role as an advance organizer.

relations.rationale: Panel-precedes-and-frames-exhibits and sequence along a route are ordinary. Indexing all evidence to a common time-zero at entry is a mild extension of what timing-and-tracking already records.

processes.rationale: Museum practice sees interpretation as cumulative meaning-making and attention as declining with fatigue. Treating interpretive change as a transient response that settles toward a steady state requires viewing the visit as convergence dynamics, a different kind of process description.

operations.rationale: Changing a panel and comparing periods, tracking routes and pauses, and interviewing through the visit are all standard. The added step of extracting temporal features from an aligned trajectory is procedural extension, not reorganization.

observables.rationale: Routes and pauses are native time series, but interview talk must be reinterpreted as samples of a scalar-like interpretation signal so that delay, rise, overshoot, and settling can be read from it. This changes what interview evidence is treated as.

inferences.rationale: Native inference is whether and how the panel shaped interpretation. Inferring onset speed, persistence, and stabilization of framing, and using trajectory shape to discriminate priming models, treats findings as dynamic properties rather than outcome differences.

failure_modes.rationale: Noise, unknown initial state, saturation, disturbances, interacting inputs, and short observation map directly onto known visitor-study confounds. The source omits the target's central threat, differing populations across periods, which must be added from target practice.

naturalization.evidence: Before/after comparison when a label is revised, timing-and-tracking of routes and stops, and studies of entrance panels as advance organizers are ordinary visitor-studies practice. There is no clear ordinary-practice example of practitioners describing within-visit interpretation using transient-response features such as overshoot or settling time.
naturalization.rationale: The experimental design and the within-visit recording would be reached for without prompting from control engineering, so the transfer is not non-native. The trajectory-feature vocabulary and the dynamics inference would not be. This mixed status keeps the case out of Native and supports Adjacent; it does not bear on Remote versus Alien.

classification.class_rationale: The core operations (change one panel, hold the rest fixed, track routes and pauses, interview through the visit, compare periods) are already ordinary practice, so inquiry is left substantially intact. The transfer reinterprets interview evidence as a time-indexed signal and reframes findings as dynamic properties (onset, persistence, settling), which is representational reinterpretation on processes, observables, and inferences but does not replace the target's evidentiary base or its question, which already asks how interpretation changes through a visit. The closest boundary is Adjacent/Remote; Remote would require the temporal-feature inferential rule to reorganize how the study is conducted, whereas here it adds an analytic layer to a design the museum would run anyway.
uncertainty: The step is applied across different visitor cohorts, not to the same system over time; whether treating each visit as a response from time-zero at entry is a legitimate counterpart to a step depends on cohort comparability, which the packet does not establish.

Interview evidence may be too sparse within a visit to support trajectory features finer than early/middle/exit; if only exit interviews exist for interpretation, the trajectory reduces to routes and pauses and the interpretation signal is unavailable rather than ungrounded.
Whether interpretation can be coded as a scalar or low-dimensional index over time is a methodological assumption; museum interpretation research often treats meaning as qualitative and plural.

The target domain 'museum interpretation' spans quantitative visitor studies and curatorial or hermeneutic practice; naturalization is judged mainly against visitor-studies practice and may be weaker for interpretive-planning specialists.
Overshoot and oscillation have weak target counterparts; they are not essential to the instrument's chain, so they do not push the class toward Alien, but their inclusion is a tension recorded here.

Grounding is partial rather than full because the interpretation-signal counterpart is constructed; if a reviewer treats it as analogy-dependent rather than a designable measurement, the case sits at a low/moderate displacement with weaker grounding, a taxonomy tension rather than grounds for Alien.

displacement.rationale: Interview evidence is reinterpreted as a sampled signal and interpretive change as a transient response with a settled level, but the design, evidence sources, and central question remain the museum's own.

grounding.rationale: The input (panel as advance organizer), the change (panel revision between periods), and behavioral trajectories (routes and pauses) have defensible target counterparts. The interpretation-over-time signal is a constructable measurement with target precedent in coded interview themes but is not yet established. Delay and exit-level difference are grounded features; overshoot and oscillation are constructed mainly to preserve source structure and lack independent target support, though they are not essential to the chain.

boundary_evidence.changes_what_is_done: Adds alignment of every visit on entry as time zero and extraction of temporal features from the aligned trajectories. Panel change, tracking, and interviewing are already done in ordinary formative evaluation.
boundary_evidence.changes_what_is_observed: Interview talk becomes samples of an interpretation signal indexed to visit time; new observables are first appearance of the panel's frame, rate of adoption, and point of stabilization. Routes and pauses remain observed as before.
boundary_evidence.changes_what_is_inferred: Shifts from whether the panel changed interpretation to how quickly the framing takes hold, whether it persists or decays, and when interpretation stabilizes, with trajectory shape used to discriminate priming models.
boundary_evidence.invented_counterparts: Overshoot as over-application of the panel frame followed by moderation, oscillation as alternation between frames, and steady state as a settled exit interpretation are constructed counterparts with little independent target grounding. None is essential to the instrument's chain, so no essential invented counterpart is identified.
